office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Three-term Rep. Joel McEntire faces a rematch with labor council president Terry Carlson, who placed first in the four-way primary 43.2% to 41.6%. McEntire was fined by the Legislative Ethics Board and placed under a protection order in September 2026 over Facebook posts.

candidates.summary: Longview timber worker and president of the Cowlitz-Wahkiakum Central Labor Council, running on affordability, infrastructure, rural healthcare and labor protections; supports the millionaires' tax.
highlights: Supports ESSB 6346, the tax on income over $1 million, while pledging to oppose taxes on working families [S4]
Would protect rural hospitals and have the state fill gaps left by federal Medicare and Medicaid cuts [S4]
Calls for cutting costs and delays that make homes more expensive to build [S4]
Endorsed by the Washington State Labor Council [S10]

taxes.basis: Supports the millionaires' income tax and says the wealthy should pay their share, while pledging to oppose taxes on working families.

spending.basis: Calls for state investment in energy, roads, broadband, ports and rural healthcare.

housing.basis: Housing plank is to build more by cutting costs and delays; no tenant-protection or public-housing plank.

climate.basis: Wants environmental protection without raising costs at the gas pump and more power generation.

healthcare.basis: Would protect rural hospitals and backfill federal Medicare and Medicaid cuts within the current system.

experience.basis: Has not held public office; labor council president and timber worker challenging a three-term incumbent.

candidates.summary: Cathlamet Marine veteran and former teacher first elected in 2020; runs on fiscal restraint and opposition to the 2025-26 tax increases. Fined by the Legislative Ethics Board in 2026 over a Facebook comment.
highlights: Calls ESSB 6346 'blatantly unconstitutional'; roll call records him excused on its final passage [S6][S16]
Says parents have a right to know what is taught in the classroom and supports school choice [S4]
Voted against ESHB 1296 and for all twelve Republican amendments to it [S17]
Sponsored 2025 laws on burrowing-shrimp research and cultural items at graduations [S10]
Fined $500 by the Legislative Ethics Board and placed under a one-year protection order over Facebook posts [S14][S15]

taxes.basis: Opposes the income tax and 2026 tax bills in repeated statements and voted against the 2025 capital gains, services and B&O tax increases.

spending.basis: Calls for living within means and 'right-sizing our government'; voted against the 2025-27 operating budget.

housing.basis: Voted against the 2025 rent and fee increase limits and the 2026 shelter-siting bill.

safety.basis: Site prioritizes supporting law enforcement; voted against state decertification of sheriffs.

climate.basis: Opposed the Forest Practices Board stream-buffer rule as driven by environmental activism; voted against the clean fuels bill.

experience.basis: Three-term incumbent with enacted bills, seeking a fourth term.

local-control.basis: Says one-size-fits-all state policy does not work; co-signed opposition to state removal of elected sheriffs.

immigration.basis: Co-signed criticism of pushing sheriffs toward non-cooperation with federal immigration authorities; voted against limits on law enforcement face coverings.

parental-rights.basis: Says parents have a right to know what is taught, voted against ESHB 1296 and for all Republican amendments, and offered parents' rights amendments in 2026.
